structured_output.text:
The question is exactly the Erdős–Szemerédi sum–product conjecture (1983), which is open: it is neither proved nor disproved that $\max(|A+A|,|AA|)\gg_\varepsilon |A|^{2-\varepsilon}$.

Sharpness of exponent 2: for $A=\{1,\dots,n\}$, $|A+A|=2n-1$ and (Ford) $|AA|\asymp n^2/((\log n)^{\delta}(\log\log n)^{3/2})$, $\delta\approx 0.086$, so $\max(|A+A|,|AA|)=o(|A|^2)$; the conjectured $|A|^{2-\varepsilon}$ is the strongest possible statement of this shape.

Rigorous partial result (Elekes): $|A+A||AA|\gg |A|^{5/2}$, hence $\max(|A+A|,|AA|)\gg |A|^{5/4}$. Proof: Let $P=(A+A)\times(AA)$, $|P|=|A+A||AA|$, and $L=\{\ell_{a,b}: y=a(x-b),\ a,b\in A, a\ne0\}$, $|L|\ge \tfrac12|A|^2$ distinct lines. Each $\ell_{a,b}$ contains the $|A|$ points $(b+c,ac)$, $c\in A$, of $P$, so $I(P,L)\ge \tfrac12|A|^3$. Szemerédi–Trotter gives $|A|^3\ll (|A+A||AA|)^{2/3}|A|^{4/3}+|A+A||AA|+|A|^2$; since $|A+A||AA|\ge|A|^2$, either the middle term dominates (then $|A+A||AA|\gg|A|^3$) or the first does (then $|A+A||AA|\gg|A|^{5/2}$). In all cases $|A+A||AA|\gg|A|^{5/2}$ and $\max\ge(|A+A||AA|)^{1/2}\gg|A|^{5/4}$.

Known results beyond this: Solymosi (2009) $\max\gg |A|^{4/3}/(\log|A|)^{1/3}$ via $|AA||A+A|^2\gg|A|^4/\log|A|$; Konyagin–Shkredov and later Rudnev–Stevens et al.: exponent $4/3+c$ for a small explicit $c>0$ (e.g. $c=2/1167$). The gap between $4/3+c$ and $2-\varepsilon$ is open.

Final answer: the statement is conjectured to be true (Erdős–Szemerédi conjecture) and exponent 2 would be optimal, but it is an open problem; I prove here only the weaker bound $\max(|A+A|,|AA|)\gg|A|^{5/4}$, and the best known bound is $|A|^{4/3+c}$.
